problem: Prior interactive/asking agents mostly target pure navigation with template questions and well-defined oracle answers (e.g. distance to goal). They do not handle vision-dialog task completion where the best next step is ambiguous and there is no oracle action, and they cannot ask free-form questions.
motivation: Household assistants must resolve ambiguities during long, multi-step tasks, so they need to decide when to ask and what to ask. Existing agents just follow instructions, or need an always-available expert (Ask4Help) or fixed templates (DialFRED).
key_idea: Add a confusion module (entropy or gradient norm) to an E.T. Actioner to decide when to ask, and use a Planner (predicted sub-goals as answers), a QA Generator (template + free-form T5 questions) and a contrastive QA Evaluator to pick what to ask.
insight: Asking when confused gives similar or better performance with far fewer questions: 44±64 questions per task vs 102±101 for a fixed every-3-steps schedule (about 57% fewer). Valid QA content matters: replacing the question with an empty string or <UNK> lowers SR/GC (16.0/19.4 to 14.4/17.6 and 13.4/16.8). Gains are small in absolute terms, though, and a user study shows only 61% step-level relevance, with ill-timed questions from using all future sub-goals as candidate answers.
method: Actioner: an Episodic Transformer that encodes utterances, visual observations and actions, with MLP heads giving action and object distributions; the E.T. checkpoint comes from the TEACh codebase.

Confusion module (entropy): triggers a question when H(p_action) > eps_a, or when H(p_object) > eps_o and the predicted action is an interaction. The question is actually asked only if entropy drops after adding the QA pair to the state.

Confusion module (gradient): uses the L2 norm of the loss gradient w.r.t. hidden state h_{t-1}, with predicted action/object as pseudo-labels (BADGE). Triggers when the norm exceeds a threshold and asks only if it decreases.

Planner: a fine-tuned T5 that takes utterances plus the action set and generates the future sub-goal sequence (interaction actions plus abstract 'Find'). Sub-goals and their nouns serve as candidate answers.

QA Generator: oracle template QAs (Location, Appearance, Direction, Current/Next Sub-goal) plus free-form QAs from a T5 question generator (SQuAD-finetuned) conditioned on history and candidate answer.

QA Evaluator: a DistilBERT QA embedding vs an MLP-projected Actioner hidden state, scored by cosine similarity and trained with a CLIP N-pair contrastive loss. The top-k pairs are ranked and one is sampled by normalized score.

setting.backbone: Episodic Transformer Actioner (pretrained TEACh weights) + T5 Planner + T5 question generator + DistilBERT QA Evaluator (all trained/fine-tuned)
setting.training_data: TEACh (over 3,000 human-human dialogues in AI2-THOR); Planner sub-goals derived from TEACh trajectories; QA Evaluator trained on TEACh QAs plus oracle-template QAs; question generator T5 finetuned on SQuAD
setting.observation: egocentric RGB frames + dialog history + action history
setting.action_space: discrete navigation actions (Forward, Turn, Pan) and interaction actions (Pickup, Slice, Open, ...) with an object argument
setting.privileged: Oracle template QAs use simulator object attributes (material, location, direction); color comes from a HSV dictionary approach

results: ELBA variants beat the E.T. baseline (seen SR 15.1 / GC 15.7; unseen SR 4.9 / GC 3.3) on all metrics, e.g. ELBA w/E reaches 19.2 seen GC and 5.7 unseen SR. Entropy-based confusion is slightly better than gradient-based. Absolute success rates remain low.
limitations: Absolute gains are small and success rates are low; the oracle answers use simulator information and the QA is generated rather than from a real human
Ill-timed and ill-formed QAs, since all future sub-goals are candidate answers and there is no question-answer consistency check; crude HSV color detection
Compared mainly with E.T. only; the user study shows just 61% step-level relevance and the seen-split TLW metrics do not improve
